## Context

Milestone 5c: the credential an agent can hold. 5b built a guard and could not switch it on, because /mcp is on the guarded mux, an MCP call is a POST, and an agent has no passkey. A token is issued at the command line, carried in a header, scoped to one path and one project, and revoked immediately.

## Done means

An agent reaches the mandated tool call on a server started with --accounts, carrying a token and no session cookie. A token is printed once and stored only as a hash; there is nothing to look up and a lost token is reissued and the old one revoked. A token can be revoked, and it stops working on the running server rather than at the next restart. A revoked token leaves its row behind, so a listing can still say it existed and when it stopped. A token is not a passkey: it opens exactly the path the server registers and nothing else, and still cannot read the records surface or sign in. The prefix it is issued with is required on presentation rather than trimmed if present, so it identifies a secret wherever one ends up. A token is scoped to a project, like every other role here; one issued for another project is refused. It carries no role, because the surface it opens serves one read-only tool and a role there would have been a choice with no effect. Rubbish in the Authorization header is refused rather than mistaken for anything, and an absent header is refused exactly as a revoked one is. The startup banner does not advertise a tool-call URL that refuses: with --accounts on it names the header, and it says when no token is live. A token id is safe to type at a shell.

## Verified against

Tests, plus the whole thing against a running server on 127.0.0.1:7951 with --accounts enforced. Measured there, in order: POST /mcp with no credential 403; with a token 200; a full MCP handshake — initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/call — returning this repository's routing in full; GET /records with the same token 303 to /signin rather than through. Then, without restarting: mustur account revoke, and the same token 403 on the same process. The listing shows the token before as last used and after as revoked. In tests: a real MCP client through the real guard rather than a bare POST, because tools/list before initialize is refused by the protocol and would have proved nothing about the guard (TestAnAgentReachesTheToolCallWithATokenAndNoCookie). Both negative tests were mutation-checked. Widening the guard's scope from /mcp to everything makes TestATokenOpensTheToolCallAndNothingElse fail; making ByToken ignore the revoked column makes TestRevokingATokenStopsItAtOnce fail. The scope test first passed for the wrong reason: its client followed the guard's 303 to /signin and reported 200 on a public page. It now follows no redirects and asserts 303 or 403 rather than not-200. The guard lets a token past /mcp with no write check, which is only safe while every tool on that surface reads. internal/mcpsrv's own test asserts exactly one tool named mustur_route and now says why, so adding a second fails there and names the guard. After the review: the prefix requirement, the exact-path scope, and the token-before-cookie precedence each got a test, and the first two were mutation-checked — trimming the prefix again and widening the path to the subtree each make their test fail. Done-when measured all five clauses independently on its own server, including that the plaintext secret is absent from the database file and from stdout.

## Risks

Nothing here is deployed. The running service passes neither --origin nor --accounts, and issuing the deployment's own token is the owner's act. A token has no expiry, deliberately: an invitation expires because it is a link in transit and a session expires because a browser is borrowed, but an agent token is configuration, and a credential that stops at 3am without anybody deciding that is an outage rather than a control. Revocation is the control and it is immediate. A token is a long-lived secret in a systemd unit or a process environment, which is a weaker place than a device's secure element. Scope is what makes that acceptable: one path, one project, no browser surface. Widening the scope later would be widening the blast radius of that weaker secret. The guard consults the token before the account, so a request carrying both a valid token and a session cookie is answered as the agent. That is deliberate on /mcp and reaches nowhere else, but it is a precedence rule rather than an obvious truth. last_used is written on every accepted call and is best-effort: a failure to record it does not refuse a valid credential. It is a convenience for deciding which of several tokens is safe to revoke, not an audit trail. Cloudflare Access is still in front and its removal is still the owner's judgement (MUS-Q-0039). This milestone removes the reason --accounts could not be turned on; it does not turn it on. Revocation is per request, so a stream opened before it survives it — MUS-F-0028, bounded because that stream is server-to-client only and carries no tool call. The token has no expiry, which contradicts the words 'with its own lifetime' in the owner's own answer on MUS-Q-0051; the argument for none is in decisions.md and the question is back with the owner as MUS-Q-0055 rather than settled by the builder. Three findings in this milestone were claims discharged against nothing: a test cited by a name that does not exist, a scope argument attributed to a question that never made it, and a one-in-thirty-two that is one in sixty-four.
